label: 2026-09-18_isaacsim_scan_binning
question: Why does Isaac Sim's /scan sit half a beam off the world manifest, when Gazebo's sits exactly on it?

publisher_contract.source: isaacsim.ros2.nodes OgnROS2PublishLaserScan.cpp publishFromGMO -> getLaserScanOutputIndex; restated in isaacsim/ros2/nodes/tests/test_rtx_sensor.py
publisher_contract.consequence: bin i spans [angle_min + i*inc, angle_min + (i+1)*inc) and is LABELLED with its lower edge, so the ray that filled it is always at or above the reported angle

ray_directions.method: same profile with rangeAccuracyM and azimuthErrorStd zeroed, in a box room of known size; the range alone fixes the true azimuth
ray_directions.conclusion: the azimuth the sensor reports IS the direction the ray went, exactly; and the 360 rays fire at exactly integer degrees, i.e. exactly ON the publisher bin boundaries

against_the_recorded_scans.method: per-beam angular offset solved individually against ranges ray-cast from worlds/small_office/world.yaml, restricted to wall beams with real angular leverage
against_the_recorded_scans.note: scan_test averages 20 scans per beam, which is why the real recorded offset is unimodal at half a beam rather than the bimodal 0-or-1 seen in a single revolution

conclusion: Isaac Sim s lidar is NOT rotated. The rays point exactly where they should. Every ray lands exactly on a publisher bin boundary, and the profile s own azimuth jitter decides which side it falls; the per-beam angular error is therefore 0 or one WHOLE beam, never half of one, and half a beam is only the mean of that coin flip.
